sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from

a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Alpelisib, a urea-linked pyrrolidine heteroaromatic with a fluorinated aryl group and a similar physicochemical profile, has human oral bioavailability of 50-68.7%, supporting F >= 20% for the query.

Brepocitinib, a heteroaromatic pyrazolopyrimidine-type kinase inhibitor, has absolute oral bioavailability of 75% with an estimated 100% fraction absorbed, supporting favorable oral absorption for the query's similar heteroaromatic scaffold.
Vernakalant, which shares the 3-hydroxypyrrolidine motif present in the query, has absolute oral bioavailability of 58-71% in fasted healthy volunteers, supporting F >= 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule itself.
Structural transfer from training contexts is qualitative; no exact structural match is present.
Solubility and first-pass metabolism are inferred from physicochemical properties rather than measured for the query.
L2 records are not yet available to further clarify absorption or formulation effects.
content.decision_summary: All L1 gold records report human oral bioavailability values of at least 46%, and the query's favorable physicochemical properties plus partial structural analogies to high-F compounds support F >= 20%; no affirmative low-F evidence is present, so the prediction is high.
